question.text: A perfectly diamagnetic sphere has a small spherical cavity at its centre, which is filled with a paramagnetic substance. The whole system is placed in a uniform magnetic field B→. Then the field inside the paramagnetic substance is:

options.text: much large than <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced close="|" open="|"><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></mfenced></math> and parallel to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></math>

much large than <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced open="|" close="|"><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></mfenced></math> but opposite to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi><mo>→</mo></mover></math>

solution.text: When magnetic field is applied diamagnetic substance produces magnetic field in opposite direction so net magnetic field will be zero.
